title: realvirtual Open Digital Twin Format (rv-ODT)
description: Machine-readable specification of the realvirtual Open Digital Twin Format. Component data is carried per glTF node under extras.realvirtual. Where the human-readable specification.md and this file disagree, this file is normative. Licensed under CC BY 4.0 (see schema/LICENSE).

ComponentReference.description: Reference to a component or PLC signal on another glTF node, identified by its scene path. The 'path' field is the ONLY identity carried today; a stable node-id field may be added alongside it in a future minor version, in which case 'path' remains valid and consumers prefer the id when both are present.

path.description: Node path identifying the target, built from glTF node NAMES. NORMATIVE RULES. (1) Root inclusion: the path is absolute and STARTS AT the exported scene root node — the root's own name is the first segment, so a reference to the root itself is exactly that name and a reference to a same-named direct child is 'X/X'. The glTF scene object itself contributes no segment. (2) Separator: '/'. glTF node names may legally contain '/', but Three.js' GLTFLoader strips it from every name it loads (see rule 3), so a conforming path is unambiguously splittable on '/'; producers MUST NOT emit a name containing '/'. (3) Which name: the node's glTF name as written in the file (nodes[i].name), BEFORE any consumer-side transformation. Three.js in particular applies PropertyBinding.sanitizeNodeName (whitespace to '_', then the reserved characters [ ] . : / removed) and then appends a '_N' suffix to make names unique FILE-GLOBALLY. Neither the sanitization nor the dedup suffix belongs in this field. (4) Uniqueness: producers SHOULD ensure paths are unique within the file; where two nodes anywhere in the file share a name, producers SHOULD warn, because consumers that dedup names will break every path leading THROUGH such a node. (5) Consumer fallbacks, permitted in this order and no other: (a) exact match on the written path; (b) match after applying the consumer's own name transformation to the query (e.g. space to '_'); (c) match against a pre-transformation alias the consumer recorded for a node it renamed, including for that node's descendants; (d) unique proper-suffix match, i.e. a registered path ending in '/' + the query. A consumer MUST NOT resolve step (d) when more than one distinct target matches — it MUST report the ambiguity and treat the reference as unresolved rather than pick one. Steps (b) to (d) are tolerance for imperfect producers, not part of the contract: a conforming producer is resolved entirely by step (a).

Vector3.description: 3D vector. Coordinate convention per field: see the 'unityCoords' vocabulary keyword.

ActiveOnly.description: Connection-state gate: whether a component participates in simulation depending on the viewer's live-connection state.

Drive.description: Linear or rotational motion control along a local axis. The base Drive component.

Direction.description: Motion axis of the drive in Unity local coordinates; 'Virtual' drives no transform.

ReverseDirection.description: Set to true if the direction needs to be inverted.

Offset.description: Start offset of the drive from zero position in millimeters or degrees.

StartPosition.description: Start position of the drive in millimeters or degrees.

TargetSpeed.description: The target speed of the drive in millimeters per second (degrees per second for rotational drives).

Acceleration.description: The acceleration in millimeters per second squared.

UseAcceleration.description: If set to true the drive uses the acceleration.

SmoothAcceleration.description: If set to true the drive uses a jerk-limited S-curve instead of the trapezoidal ramp; requires UseAcceleration.

Jerk.description: The jerk in millimeters per second cubed (degrees per second cubed for rotational drives); only used with SmoothAcceleration.

SpeedOverride.description: Speed override factor for this drive, multiplied with the global speed override.

JumpToLowerLimitOnUpperLimit.description: If set to true the drive wraps around at its limits instead of stopping: passing the upper limit continues at the lower limit and vice versa.

UseLimits.description: If set to true the drive motion is limited to the range between LowerLimit and UpperLimit.

LowerLimit.description: Lower drive limit in millimeters or degrees.

UpperLimit.description: Upper drive limit in millimeters or degrees.

JogForward.description: Jog the drive continuously forward at TargetSpeed.

JogBackward.description: Jog the drive continuously backward at TargetSpeed.

TargetPosition.description: The destination position of the drive in millimeters or degrees.

Drive_Simple.description: Drive behavior: simple jog control with speed and directional bits plus feedback signals.

Speed.description: PLC output for the speed of the drive in millimeters per second; can be scaled by ScaleSpeed.

Accelaration.description: PLC output for the acceleration of the drive in millimeters per second squared; field name keeps the original C# spelling.

Forward.description: Signal to move the drive forward.

Backward.description: Signal to move the drive backward.

IsAtPosition.description: Signal for the current position of the drive in millimeters.

IsAtSpeed.description: Signal for the current speed of the drive in millimeters per second.

IsDriving.description: Signal is true while the drive is driving.

Enable.description: Optional motion enable. False stops the drive immediately and ignores Forward/Backward; true follows the current Forward/Backward levels again. Unset means always enabled.

ScaleSpeed.description: Scale factor for the input and output speed and acceleration.

CurrentPositionScale.description: Scale factor for the current position feedback.

CurrentPositionOffset.description: Offset applied to the position feedback in millimeters.

ScaleFeedbackPosition.description: If true, applies scale and offset to the position feedback.

Drive_Cylinder.description: Drive behavior: two-position pneumatic/hydraulic cylinder with in/out command and end-position feedback.

MinPos.description: Minimum position of the cylinder in millimeters.

MaxPos.description: Maximum position of the cylinder in millimeters.

TimeOut.description: Time for moving out from minimum to maximum position in seconds.

TimeIn.description: Time for moving in from maximum to minimum position in seconds.

OneBitCylinder.description: If set to true only one bit controls the cylinder; when Out is false the cylinder moves in.

InvertOutputLogic.description: When true, inverts the Out/In signal logic (Out=false extends, Out=true retracts).

Mode.description: Valve mode. Legacy: Out/In commands are latched (OneBitCylinder/InvertOutputLogic apply). DoubleActing (5/3 valve): moves only while Out or In is on, holds when both are off or both on. SingleActingPositive: Out on moves to MaxPos, off returns to MinPos. SingleActingNegative: Out on moves to MinPos, off returns to MaxPos. The new modes ignore OneBitCylinder and InvertOutputLogic.

Out.description: Signal for moving the cylinder out.

In.description: Signal for moving the cylinder in.

IsOut.description: Signal is true when the cylinder is out or stopped by the Max sensor.

IsIn.description: Signal is true when the cylinder is in or stopped by the Min sensor.

IsMax.description: Signal is true when the cylinder is at the maximum position.

IsMin.description: Signal is true when the cylinder is at the minimum position.

IsMovingOut.description: Signal is true while the cylinder is moving out.

IsMovingIn.description: Signal is true while the cylinder is moving in.

Enable.description: Optional motion enable. False stops and holds the cylinder; Out/In commands are latched and executed when it turns true again. Unset means always enabled.

Drive_Speed.description: Drive behavior: speed-controlled motion via PLC target-speed signal with speed/position feedback.

SignalTargetSpeed.description: Target (maximum) speed of the drive in millimeters per second.

SignalAcceleration.description: Acceleration of the drive in millimeters per second squared.

SignalCurrentSpeed.description: Signal for the current drive speed in millimeters per second.

SignalCurrentPosition.description: Signal for the current drive position in millimeters.

SignalIsDriving.description: Signal is true while the drive is driving.

TargetSpeed.description: Default target speed in millimeters per second when no signal is wired.

Acceleration.description: Default acceleration in millimeters per second squared when no signal is wired.

CurrentPositionScale.description: Scale factor for the current position feedback.

CurrentPositionOffset.description: Offset applied to the position feedback in millimeters.

ScaleFeedbackPosition.description: If true, applies scale and offset to the position feedback.

Drive_SEWMovilink.description: Drive behavior: SEW-EURODRIVE MOVILINK unit profile. The PLC writes control word 1 and a speed setpoint, the drive returns status word 1 and the actual speed.

ControlWord1.description: MOVILINK control word 1 (PO1). Bit 0 is the inverted controller inhibit, bits 1 and 2 are active low, bit 6 is the fault reset.

SpeedSetpoint.description: MOVILINK speed setpoint (PO2), encoded as selected by Encoding.

StatusWord1.description: MOVILINK status word 1 (PI1) written back to the PLC every tick.

SpeedActual.description: MOVILINK actual speed (PI2) written back to the PLC every tick.

MaxSpeed.description: Drive speed in millimeters per second (or degrees per second) at 100 percent of the maximum speed.

Encoding.description: Speed setpoint encoding: SPEED[%] with 0x4000 = 100 percent, or SPEED with 0.2 rpm per bit.

MaxSpeedRpm.description: Maximum speed in rpm, used to convert the 0.2 rpm per bit encoding to a fraction.

Acceleration.description: Drive acceleration in millimeters per second squared (or degrees per second squared).

SimulateFault.description: If true the drive reports a fault in status word bit 5 until the PLC acknowledges with control word bit 6.

FaultCode.description: Fault code reported in the status word high byte while a fault is active.

Drive_Gear.description: Drive behavior: slaves this node's Drive to a master Drive position with gear ratio and offset.

MasterDrive.description: Master drive which defines the position of this drive.

GearFactor.description: Gear factor between master and slave position.

Offset.description: Offset of the gear in millimeters.

Drive_FollowPosition.description: Drive behavior: directly follows a PLC position signal (no ramping) with position feedback.

Position.description: Signal (PLC output) for the commanded position of the drive.

CurrentPosition.description: PLC input for the current position of the drive (without offset and scaling).

Offset.description: Offset in millimeters added to the position signal.

Scale.description: Scale factor applied to the position value.

CurrentPositionScale.description: Scale factor for the current position feedback.

ScaleFeedbackPosition.description: If true, applies scale and offset to the position feedback.

Drive_DestinationMotor.description: Drive behavior: point-to-point positioning motor. Start command drives to a destination with speed/acceleration commands and rich feedback.

StartDrive.description: Start-to-drive signal; a value change starts motion towards Destination.

Destination.description: Destination position of the drive in millimeters.

TargetSpeed.description: Target (maximum) speed of the drive in millimeters per second.

Acceleration.description: Acceleration of the drive in millimeters per second squared.

IsAtPosition.description: Signal for the current position of the drive in millimeters.

IsAtSpeed.description: Signal for the current drive speed in millimeters per second.

IsAtDestination.description: Signal is true when the drive is at the destination.

IsDriving.description: Signal is true while the drive is currently driving.

CurrentPositionScale.description: Scale factor for the current position feedback.

CurrentPositionOffset.description: Offset applied to the position command and feedback in millimeters.

ScaleFeedbackPosition.description: If true, applies scale and offset to the position feedback.

Drive_PositionSwitch.description: Drive behavior: boolean output signal that is true while the drive position is inside configured areas.

OutputSignal.description: Output signal to the PLC; true when the drive position is inside any configured area (inverted when InvertAreas is true).

InvertAreas.description: If true, areas define false zones instead of true zones (inverts the output).

PositionOffset.description: Global offset in millimeters or degrees applied to the drive position before area checking.

Drive_ErraticPosition.description: Drive behavior: moves the drive to random (or alternating min/max) positions — demo/test motion.

MinPos.description: Minimum position of the range where the drive is allowed to move to, in millimeters.

MaxPos.description: Maximum position of the range where the drive is allowed to move to, in millimeters.

Speed.description: Speed of the drive in millimeters per second.

IterateBetweenMaxAndMin.description: If true the drive only iterates between MinPos and MaxPos; if false it moves to random positions.

SignalEnable.description: While this signal is true the drive moves to erratic positions; when unwired it is always enabled.

Drive_ContinousDestination.description: Drive behavior: intelligent positioning drive that moves to a destination whenever the destination value changes - no separate start signal, unlike Drive_DestinationMotor.

Destination.description: Target destination position in millimeters when no signal is wired.

Acceleration.description: Drive acceleration in millimeters per second squared when no signal is wired.

TargetSpeed.description: Maximum drive speed in millimeters per second when no signal is wired.

CurrentPositionScale.description: Scale factor applied to the destination command and the position feedback.

CurrentPositionOffset.description: Offset applied to the destination command and the position feedback in millimeters.

ScaleFeedbackPosition.description: If true, applies scale and offset to the position feedback.

SignalDestination.description: Destination position of the drive in millimeters; a value change starts the move.

SignalAcceleration.description: Acceleration of the drive in millimeters per second squared.

SignalTargetSpeed.description: Target (maximum) speed of the drive in millimeters per second.

SignalIsAtPosition.description: Signal for the current position of the drive in millimeters.

SignalIsAtSpeed.description: Signal for the current drive speed in millimeters per second.

SignalIsAtDestination.description: Signal is true when the drive is at the destination.

SignalIsDriving.description: Signal is true while the drive is currently driving.

DrivePulseEncoder.description: Drive add-on: incremental pulse encoder. Toggles a bool signal every time the drive position passes another PulseIntervall. Sits on a Drive node next to any Drive_* behavior.

PulseIntervall.description: Distance in millimeters (or degrees) between two pulses. 0 disables the encoder.

Offset.description: Position in millimeters (or degrees) of the first pulse.

PulseEncoderSignal.description: Toggled each time the drive passes the next pulse position.

Drive_ProfidriveSpeed.description: Drive behavior: PROFIdrive speed-controlled drive (SINAMICS) on standard telegram 1. The PLC writes control word STW1 and the normalized speed setpoint NSOLL_A; the drive runs the PROFIdrive state machine and returns status word ZSW1 and the actual speed NIST_A.

ReferenceSpeed.description: Drive speed in millimeters per second (or degrees per second) at the full-scale setpoint (100 percent), the reference speed p2000.

SetpointScale.description: Raw setpoint value that equals 100 percent. PROFIdrive NSOLL_A = 16384 (0x4000); ABB Drives profile REF1 = 20000.

Acceleration.description: Drive acceleration in millimeters per second squared (or degrees per second squared).

SimulateFault.description: If true the drive reports a fault (ZSW1.3) until the PLC acknowledges with a rising edge of STW1.7.

SimulateWarning.description: If true the drive reports a warning (ZSW1.7).

SpeedSetpoint.description: Normalized speed setpoint NSOLL_A (SetpointScale = 100 percent of ReferenceSpeed, negative reverses).

StatusWord.description: PROFIdrive status word ZSW1 written back to the PLC every tick.

SpeedActual.description: Normalized actual speed NIST_A written back to the PLC every tick.

Drive_ProfidrivePos.description: Drive behavior: PROFIdrive positioning drive (SINAMICS EPOS) on telegram 111. The PLC writes STW1, POS_STW1/2, OVERRIDE, MDI_TARPOS and MDI_VELOCITY; the drive runs the PROFIdrive state machine with MDI positioning, setup mode, jog and homing and returns ZSW1, POS_ZSW1/2, XIST_A and NIST_B.

PositionScale.description: Drive millimeters (or degrees) per length unit (LU), used for MDI_TARPOS and XIST_A.

PositionOffset.description: Offset in millimeters (or degrees) applied to the position command and feedback.

VelocityScale.description: Drive speed in millimeters per second per MDI_VELOCITY unit (MDI_VELOCITY is given in 1000 LU/min).

ReferenceSpeed.description: Drive speed in millimeters per second (or degrees per second) at NIST_B = 0x40000000 (100 percent), the reference speed p2000.

JogSpeed.description: Jog speed in millimeters per second for jog 1 / jog 2 (STW1.8 / STW1.9).

Acceleration.description: Drive acceleration in millimeters per second squared (or degrees per second squared) at 100 percent override.

SimulateFault.description: If true the drive reports a fault (ZSW1.3) until the PLC acknowledges with a rising edge of STW1.7.

SimulateWarning.description: If true the drive reports a warning (ZSW1.7).

PosControlWord1.description: POS_STW1 - positioning control word 1 (PZD2): MDI mode, absolute/relative, direction, continuous transfer, setup.

PosControlWord2.description: POS_STW2 - positioning control word 2 (PZD3): set reference point, incremental jog.

MdiTargetPosition.description: MDI_TARPOS - target position in length units (PZD6+7).

StatusWord.description: ZSW1 - status word 1 (PZD1) written back to the PLC every tick.

PosStatusWord1.description: POS_ZSW1 - positioning status word 1 (PZD2); mirrors ZSW1 in this model.

PosStatusWord2.description: POS_ZSW2 - positioning status word 2 (PZD3): traverses forwards/backwards, traversing command active.

PositionActual.description: XIST_A - actual position in length units (PZD6+7).

SpeedActual.description: NIST_B - actual speed (PZD8+9), 0x40000000 = 100 percent of ReferenceSpeed.

Drive_FestoFHPP.description: Drive behavior: Festo Handling and Positioning Profile (FHPP) for CMMT / CMMO / CMMP controllers. The PLC writes the 8-byte FHPP output image (CCON, CPOS, record number or CDIR, velocity, target position); the drive returns SCON, SPOS, the record/SDIR echo and the actual position. Supports Record Select and Direct mode, jog and homing.

PositionScale.description: Drive millimeters (or degrees) per position increment (Direct mode target and actual position).

PositionOffset.description: Offset in millimeters (or degrees) applied to the position command and feedback.

BaseVelocity.description: Drive speed in millimeters per second at 100 percent velocity (Direct mode velocity byte = 0..100 percent).

JogSpeed.description: Jog speed in millimeters per second for CPOS.JOGP / CPOS.JOGN.

Acceleration.description: Drive acceleration in millimeters per second squared (or degrees per second squared).

Records.description: Traversing record table for Record Select mode: array of { Position, Velocity, Relative }. Byte 2 (RecordOrCdir) selects the record index.

SimulateFault.description: If true the drive reports a fault (SCON.FAULT) until the PLC acknowledges with a rising edge of CCON.RESET.

SimulateWarning.description: If true the drive reports a warning (SCON.WARN).

Ccon.description: FHPP control byte CCON (byte 0): ENABLE, STOP, RESET, OPM.

Cpos.description: FHPP control byte CPOS (byte 1): HALT, START, HOM, JOGP, JOGN.

RecordOrCdir.description: Byte 2 - record number (Record Select) or CDIR (Direct mode).

VelocityPercent.description: Byte 3 - velocity 0..100 percent of BaseVelocity (Direct mode).

TargetPosition.description: Bytes 4-7 - target position in increments (Direct mode, 32-bit signed).

Scon.description: FHPP status byte SCON (byte 0) written back to the PLC every tick.

Spos.description: FHPP status byte SPOS (byte 1) written back to the PLC every tick.

RecordOrSdir.description: Byte 2 - active record number echo (Record Select) or SDIR (Direct mode).

PositionActual.description: Bytes 4-7 - actual position in increments (32-bit signed).

Drive_UniDriveMotor.description: Drive behavior: UniDrive-style positioning controller. A Run release gates all motion, StartPositioning moves to integer setpoints (position, speed, acceleration ramp) and JogPlus / JogMinus jog with setup or manual speed; ready, referenced, in-position and integer actual position / speed are written back.

PositionScale.description: Scale factor between integer position units (PLC) and millimeters (or degrees) on the drive.

PositionOffset.description: Offset applied to the position command and feedback in millimeters (or degrees).

SpeedScale.description: Scale factor between integer speed units (PLC) and millimeters per second on the drive.

AccelerationScale.description: Scale factor between integer acceleration units (PLC) and millimeters per second squared on the drive.

SetupSpeed.description: Reduced jog speed in millimeters per second used while SpeedSelection is false.

Ready.description: If true the drive reports ready. Set to false to simulate a not-ready drive.

Referenced.description: If true the drive reports the encoder as referenced. Set to false to simulate a not-referenced drive.

Run.description: General release of the drive - while false the drive is held stopped.

StartCalibration.description: Start encoder calibration - interface completeness only, no effect in simulation.

SpeedSelection.description: Jog speed selection: false uses SetupSpeed, true uses the commanded SetSpeed.

StartPositioning.description: Start positioning to SetPosition - a rising edge triggers the move.

ResetFault.description: Fault acknowledge - interface completeness only, no effect in simulation.

SetPosition.description: Target position setpoint in integer units, scaled by PositionScale and PositionOffset.

SetSpeed.description: Target speed setpoint in integer units, scaled by SpeedScale.

SetAcceleration.description: Acceleration ramp setpoint in integer units, scaled by AccelerationScale.

SetDeceleration.description: Deceleration ramp setpoint - read for transparency, the drive brakes with the symmetric acceleration ramp.

IsReady.description: Feedback that the drive is ready, driven by the Ready setting.

IsReferenced.description: Feedback that the encoder is referenced, driven by the Referenced setting.

IsAtPosition1.description: Feedback that the commanded position has been reached (not while jogging).

ActualPosition.description: Actual drive position in integer units, scaled from the current position.

ActualSpeed.description: Actual drive speed in integer units, scaled from the current speed.

Drive_ProportionalValve.description: Drive behavior: hydraulic (or electric) proportional directional valve. An analog setpoint (+-10 V, 4-20 mA, 0-100 percent) is scaled to a -1..1 command, passed through dead band, optional hysteresis, spool response time and a flow characteristic, and applied as a signed drive speed.

Setpoint.description: Analog command setpoint in raw signal units (volts, mA or percent) when no signal is wired.

SetpointZero.description: Raw signal value for zero flow / neutral spool position (e.g. 0 for +-10 V, 12 for 4-20 mA).

SetpointFull.description: Raw signal value for 100 percent flow in forward direction (e.g. 10 for +-10 V, 20 for 4-20 mA, 100 for 0-100 percent).

Deadband.description: Dead band as a fraction (0..0.9) of the command around the neutral position, modelling spool overlap.

EnableHysteresis.description: If true, command changes smaller than Hysteresis are ignored (the spool sticks).

Hysteresis.description: Hysteresis band as a fraction (0..0.5) of the command.

FlowExponent.description: Flow characteristic exponent mapping the normalized spool position (0..1) to normalized flow: 1 = linear, greater than 1 = progressive, less than 1 = degressive. Replaces the Unity AnimationCurve, which does not travel through the GLB.

ResponseTime.description: Time in seconds for the spool to travel from neutral to full deflection (amplifier ramp plus spool dynamics). 0 = instant.

MaxSpeed.description: Drive speed in millimeters per second (or degrees per second) at 100 percent flow.

Acceleration.description: Drive acceleration in millimeters per second squared (or degrees per second squared).

SignalSetpoint.description: Analog valve setpoint from the PLC (+-10 V, 4-20 mA or percent).

SignalSpoolPosition.description: Actual spool position feedback (-1..1, 1 = full forward flow).

SignalCurrentSpeed.description: Current drive speed in millimeters per second (or degrees per second).

SignalCurrentPosition.description: Current drive position in millimeters (or degrees).

Sensor.description: Presence sensor. Collision mode uses AABB overlap; raycast mode casts a ray and reports MU hits.

LimitSensorToTag.description: Detects only MUs with this tag or name. Empty detects all MUs.

ShowGizmo.description: Displays the sensor detection volume in the web viewer. Detection stays active when hidden.

UseRaycast.description: If true the sensor uses raycast mode instead of collider (AABB overlap) mode.

RayCastDirection.description: Raycast direction vector in Unity local coordinates (readers negate X in glTF space).

SensorOccupied.description: Boolean PLC input for the sensor signal; true when the sensor is occupied.

SensorNotOccupied.description: Boolean PLC input for the sensor; true when the sensor is NOT occupied.

AutoRay.description: Derives the ray beam from the node bounding box (naming-convention sensors).

PhysicsMode.description: If true and the sensor overlaps a physics zone, the sensor is physics-managed: collision mode uses a physics sensor collider (enter/leave events), raycast mode a physics raycast. Physics-managed sensors detect only physics-owned MUs; sensors that must detect kinematic MUs keep the default false.

Mode.description: Legacy mode string ('Raycast'/'Collision'); readers SHOULD convert it to UseRaycast when UseRaycast is absent.

TransportSurface.description: Conveyor surface that moves MUs along a direction at the referenced Drive's speed.

TransportDirection.description: Transport direction in Unity local coordinates, set by the Drive component at export (readers negate X in glTF space).

Radial.description: If true the surface transports radially around the drive axis (turntables).

TextureScale.description: Texture animation speed multiplier in texture units per meter.

HeightOffsetOverride.description: Manual override for the transport height offset in millimeters.

AnimateSurface.description: Enables texture animation to visualize surface movement.

DriveReference.description: Optional drive reference for special cases; normally empty to use the auto-detected parent drive.

Accumulate.description: If true MUs on this surface accumulate: each MU clamps its advance to the free distance up to the next MU in move direction (no penetration). Ignored on Radial surfaces.

MinGap.description: Minimum front gap in millimeters kept between accumulated MUs.

PhysicsMode.description: If true and the surface lies fully inside a physics zone, the surface runs in physics mode: a kinematic conveyor body carries MUs via friction and jams/stacking are simulated physically. Ignored on Radial surfaces (v1 exclusion) and when the deployment switch simulation.physicsSurfaceDefault is false.

Source.description: Spawns new MU (Movable Unit) instances at intervals or by distance to the last spawned MU.

GenerateMU.description: Generates one MU on a false-to-true transition, including an initial true value.

DeleteAllMU.description: Deletes this source's MUs on a false-to-true transition.

StartInterval.description: Delay before the first interval generation.

RandomDistance.description: Randomizes the distance threshold after automatic generation.

LimitNumber.description: Limits the total number generated by this source.

MaxNumberMUs.description: Maximum lifetime generated count when LimitNumber is enabled.

SourceGenerate.description: PLCOutputBool: generates one MU on a rising edge and disables automatic distance generation at startup.

SourceGenerateOnDistance.description: PLCOutputBool: controls AutomaticGeneration by signal level.

AutomaticGeneration.description: Automatic generation of MUs when the last MU is farther than GenerateIfDistance from the source.

Interval.description: Interval in seconds between the generation of MUs; 0 disables interval generation.

GenerateIfDistance.description: Distance in millimeters from the source at which new MUs are generated.

PlaceOnTransportSurface.description: If true newly spawned MUs are placed onto the transport surface below the source.

ThisObjectAsMU.description: Name of the GameObject used as the MU prototype; defaults to this node when empty.

CollisionRoleForMUs.description: Collision role assigned to every MU spawned by this source. 'None' = spawned MUs take part in no collision check.

Spawn.description: Legacy spawn-mode hint consumed by the reference implementation's spawn-config derivation.

Sink.description: Destroys MUs that touch it. Carries no configuration fields in v1.

DeleteOnlyTag.description: Only deletes MUs with this tag; empty accepts all tags.

Grip.description: Gripper for pick-and-place: picks MUs in range on a pick signal and places them on a place signal.

GripRange.description: Search radius in millimeters for automatic MU detection when no sensor is assigned.

OneBitControl.description: If true a single signal controls the gripper (rising edge picks, falling edge places).

PlaceMode.description: Controls how MUs are released on place: Auto (context-dependent), Static (stays kinematic) or Physics (falls onto surface).

GripTargetSearchRadius.description: Search radius in millimeters for finding the nearest GripTarget on place.

PartToGrip.description: Sensor identifying the MU to be gripped; when empty, auto-detection uses GripRange.

GripTarget.description: Placement marker for precise MU positioning during Grip auto-place.

AlignPosition.description: If true the MU position is snapped to the GripTarget position when placed.

AlignRotation.description: If true the MU rotation is aligned to the GripTarget rotation when placed.

LoadOnCarrier.description: If true a Grip places the part at this pose as a load of the MU below it instead of on the target; the target stays free.

ConnectSignal.description: One-way signal bridge: copies the value of the referenced source signal onto this node's own signal.

ConnectedSignal.description: Source signal whose value is copied onto this node's own signal on every change.

Lamp.description: Signal lamp: drives the emissive color of its first child mesh from a PLC signal.

SignalLampOn.description: Bool signal driving the on state.

SingalLampFlashing.description: Bool signal driving the flashing state. Field name keeps the Unity spelling.

Intensity.description: HDR emission intensity multiplier applied to OnColor.

Flashing.description: Lamp flashes instead of holding steady.

Period.description: Flashing period in seconds; half on, half off.

LampOn.description: On state used when no signal is bound.

OnColor.description: Unity Color {r,g,b,a} (floats 0..1) for the lit state; read raw (no schema field type for colors).

SceneButtonBase.description: Click/hover state machine of a 3D scene button. Sits on the node that carries the collider in Unity (OnMouseDown) and drives its SceneButtonMoveable cap. Field names keep the Unity camelCase spelling.

moveable.description: SceneButtonMoveable this state machine animates and lights (wire componentType realvirtual.SceneButtonMoveable).

autoLight.description: Light follows the button's own active state. Wrappers set it to false when a lightSignal drives the light instead.

isToggle.description: Button latches on click instead of releasing after simpleClickTime.

simpleClickTime.description: Hold time of a non-toggle (momentary) click before the button releases again.

SceneButtonMoveable.description: Animated cap of a 3D scene button: press/rotate offset along an axis plus the lit/unlit material pair. Field names keep the Unity camelCase spelling.

axis.description: Local movement axis of the cap; translation direction, or rotation axis when angularMovement is set.

moveSpeed.description: Exponential approach rate of the cap towards its offset target (per second).

hoverOffset.description: Additional offset applied while the pointer hovers the button (metres, or degrees when angularMovement is set).

activeOffset.description: Offset the cap holds while the button is active (metres, or degrees when angularMovement is set).

mirrorHoverOffset.description: Invert the hover offset while the button is active (handle switches that flip the other way).

angularMovement.description: Rotate the cap around axis by offset degrees instead of translating it.

baseMaterial.description: Unity material descriptor {name, assetPath, shader} of the unlit state; read raw. Only the name is used - equal base/active names mean the button has no light.

activeMaterial.description: Unity material descriptor {name, assetPath, shader} of the lit state; read raw. Only the name is used - equal base/active names mean the button has no light.

renderer.description: Unity MeshRenderer reference of the cap; read raw and ignored - the cap mesh is found by traversing the node.

currentOffset.description: Unity runtime state (current animated offset); read raw and ignored - the viewer keeps its own.

PushButton3D.description: 3D push button: writes a PLCInputBool while pressed (momentary or latching) and lights its cap either from its own state or from a PLCOutputBool. Field names keep the Unity camelCase spelling.

stateSignal.description: Bool signal written by the operator click.

lightSignal.description: Bool signal driving the button light. Unset = the light follows the button's own state.

label.description: Button caption. Rendered only where the model carries a text mesh; otherwise informational.

timer.description: Hold time of a momentary click before the button releases again (ignored when toggle is set).

toggle.description: Button latches on click instead of releasing after timer.

activeOnStart.description: Button clicks itself once when the scene is ready.

EmergencyButton3D.description: 3D emergency-stop button: latching mushroom head writing a PLCInputBool. Comfort trigger/status only - never a substitute for a hard-wired emergency stop.

stateSignal.description: Bool signal written by the operator click.

activeOnStart.description: Button clicks itself once when the scene is ready.

NormallyClosed.description: If true the signal is true while the button is released (OK) and false while it is pressed, like a normally-closed emergency-stop contact.

HandleSwitch3D.description: 3D handle switch: latching lever writing a PLCInputBool.

stateSignal.description: Bool signal written by the operator click.

activeOnStart.description: Switch clicks itself once when the scene is ready.

EnergyChain.description: Turns a rigid CAD energy-chain (cable carrier) mesh into an animated chain: straight strand, half-circle bend travelling at half the follower speed, constant length. Drive axis, bend radius, link height and chain length are MEASURED from the CAD rest pose; every numeric field left at 0 means auto-calibrate.

Anchor.description: Node the fixed chain end is attached to (Unity: public Transform Anchor, wire componentType UnityEngine.Transform). Empty = auto. Shown read-only; corrected via web_editor_set_field.

Follower.description: Node the moving chain end (the carrier) is attached to. Empty = auto. Shown read-only; corrected via web_editor_set_field.

BendRadius.description: Centerline bend radius. 0 = measure from the rest pose.

ChainLength.description: Total centerline length. 0 = measure from the rest pose.

Axis.description: Travel axis in the chain-local frame. Auto = longest AABB extent.

BendUp.description: Moving strand runs above the fixed one. Flip when the measured assignment is upside down.

Bones.description: Bone count of the runtime rig. Clamped up to the minimum derived from the 15 deg linear-blend-skinning limit (21); the clamp is reported in the status line.

Enabled.description: Animate the chain. Off leaves it in the CAD rest pose.

Chain.description: Continuous chain transport: N identical elements riding a spline, all moved by one Drive (Unity realvirtual.Chain). The curve is exported as an arc-length equidistant sample table in 'Spline'; the viewer clones the 'ChainElement' template 'NumberOfElements' times and poses every clone from the drive position. Positions and lengths are millimetres, the sample table is metres in the chain node's local frame.

ConnectedDrive.description: Drive that moves the whole chain. Unresolvable: the elements are placed at their start positions and never move.

chainOrientation.description: Vertical applies Unity's tangent-side flip of the element up vector (tangent.z < 0, or tangent.z == 0 and tangent.x > 0).

NumberOfElements.description: Number of chain elements to build from the template. 0 builds nothing.

StartPosition.description: Position of the FIRST element along the chain.

CalculatedDeltaPosition.description: Derive the element spacing from the chain length divided by NumberOfElements instead of using DeltaPosition.

DeltaPosition.description: Manual spacing between two consecutive elements. Ignored while CalculatedDeltaPosition is set.

ScaledOnFixedLength.description: Scale the position fraction over FixedLength instead of the real arc length. The sample table always stays tied to the real length, so a shorter FixedLength makes the chain cycle faster over the same geometry (Unity parity).

FixedLength.description: The length the position fraction is scaled over while ScaledOnFixedLength is set.

ChainElement.description: The element template node (wire componentType UnityEngine.Transform). Cloned NumberOfElements times at load; unresolvable makes the chain inert.

NameChainElement.description: Base name of the generated elements. Children called '<name>_<n>' are treated as stale editor-generated elements and dropped before cloning; empty falls back to the template's node name.

Spline.description: Baked curve: { closed: boolean, length: number (metres), samples: number[] }. 'samples' is flat [px,py,pz, tx,ty,tz, ux,uy,uz] per sample, arc-length equidistant, in the chain node's LOCAL frame. Fewer than two samples makes the chain inert. rv-chain-path.ts is the executable TS-SSOT for this shape.

ChainElement.description: Per-element configuration of a Chain, authored on the element TEMPLATE node (Unity realvirtual.ChainElement). It carries no behaviour of its own in the viewer: the owning Chain reads these fields and poses every clone, mirroring Unity's batch update.

AlignWithChain.description: Align the element with the chain tangent while moving. Off leaves the template rotation untouched and only the position is written.

AlignVector.description: Additional up reference for the alignment. Unused on the Unity-spline path, where the baked up vectors of the sample table are authoritative; kept so the field round-trips.

InitialPosition.description: Initial position of this element along the chain. Set by the Chain for generated elements.

OffsetToDrivePosition.description: Position offset of every element relative to the drive position.

RibbonRoller.description: A roller the web (endless material: paper, film, foil, textile, sheet coil) runs over. Purely geometric: radius, rotation axis and the side the web lies on. Every roller of one RibbonPath must have a parallel axis (2 deg tolerance); the path solves the classic two-circle tangent problem in the plane perpendicular to it. The roller turns at omega = v / r, so a small idler spins faster than a large one, exactly as in the machine.

RadiusMm.description: Contact radius of the roller. 0 measures it from the mesh bounds in the plane perpendicular to Axis, in the node's own local frame, so a scaled parent does not distort it.

Axis.description: Local rotation axis of the roller and the common axis of the web path.

RibbonSide.description: Which side of the roller the web runs on. Leave it on Auto: for every normal machine Auto picks the short wrap, the only one a real web can take. Set Left or Right by hand only for an S-wrap or a wrap of more than 180 degrees, where the short wrap is the wrong one. Left and Right are the turning sense seen looking along +Axis - Left counter-clockwise, Right clockwise. Default Auto.

RotationDirection.description: Ignored. Rotation follows the resolved web contact and roller axis automatically. Set the drive direction to match the contact when authoring a driven roller.

SpinMode.description: How the roller shows that it is turning. Transform turns the roller object itself. Texture leaves the object standing still and scrolls the pattern on its barrel instead - it looks the same at a glance and costs no per-frame work, which is worth having on a machine with many idlers. Texture works only on a roller WITHOUT a drive; a driven roller is always turned by its drive. Default Transform.

MantleMesh.description: Which part scrolls in SpinMode Texture - normally the barrel of the roller. Leave it empty: the roller's own mesh is used, or the largest textured part under it that is not inside a Faces group, so the end discs stay still. Wire componentType UnityEngine.Transform (the schema convention for a node reference).

MantleMaterialName.description: Name of a material of the ribbon material library (Unity: Resources/realvirtual/RibbonMaterialLibrary). In realvirtual WEB the name is resolved against the materials of the LOADED document - exactly, then ignoring case, first match wins. Unity writes the library material into the exported GLB under exactly this name, so a document exported from Unity always resolves. Empty = not used. It is applied to the barrel only while OverrideMaterials is true.

FaceMaterialName.description: Name of a material of the ribbon material library (Unity: Resources/realvirtual/RibbonMaterialLibrary). In realvirtual WEB the name is resolved against the materials of the LOADED document - exactly, then ignoring case, first match wins. Unity writes the library material into the exported GLB under exactly this name, so a document exported from Unity always resolves. Empty = not used. It is applied to every renderer under a child named Faces, only while OverrideMaterials is true.

OverrideMaterials.description: Overrides the CAD materials of MantleMesh (MantleMaterialName) and of every renderer under a Faces child (FaceMaterialName) at simulation start; restored at stop. An empty name leaves that part unchanged. Default false.

RibbonWinder.description: An unwinder or rewinder at one end of a RibbonPath: a roller whose radius grows or shrinks with the wound length, R(L) = sqrt(CoreRadiusMm^2 + L * RibbonThicknessMm / pi). It must be the FIRST or the LAST entry of the path's Rollers list; in the middle it is inert with a warning. The wound roll is shown by scaling RollMesh radially in the two axes perpendicular to Axis, so a CAD roll needs no remodelling and no geometry is rebuilt per tick.

RadiusMm.description: Measured outer radius of the authored roll. 0 measures it from the mesh bounds; it is the reference the wound roll is scaled against and, with InitialWoundLengthMm = -1, the source of the initial length.

Axis.description: Local winding axis. Must be parallel to every other roller axis of the path.

RibbonSide.description: Side the web leaves or enters the roll on; the wrap orientation seen along +Axis.

WrapDeg.description: How far the web is shown wrapping the roll BEFORE it reaches the running tangent (an unwinder) or AFTER it leaves it (a rewinder), so the band starts/ends visibly on the roll surface instead of at the tangent point in mid-air. 0 (default) reproduces the plan-459/460 behaviour exactly - no arc at the path ends. Ignored on a winder that is not the first or the last entry of any RibbonPath.

RotationDirection.description: Ignored. Rotation follows the resolved web contact and roller axis automatically. Set the drive direction to match the contact when authoring a driven roller.

SpinMode.description: How the winder shows that it is turning; see RibbonRoller.SpinMode. A winder that carries a drive is always turned by it, so Texture only applies to a dragged reel. Default Transform.

MantleMesh.description: Which part scrolls in SpinMode Texture; see RibbonRoller.MantleMesh. Leave it empty to use the winder's own mesh. Wire componentType UnityEngine.Transform (the schema convention for a node reference).

MantleMaterialName.description: Name of a material of the ribbon material library (Unity: Resources/realvirtual/RibbonMaterialLibrary). In realvirtual WEB the name is resolved against the materials of the LOADED document - exactly, then ignoring case, first match wins. Unity writes the library material into the exported GLB under exactly this name, so a document exported from Unity always resolves. Empty = not used. It is applied to the barrel only while OverrideMaterials is true.

FaceMaterialName.description: Name of a material of the ribbon material library (Unity: Resources/realvirtual/RibbonMaterialLibrary). In realvirtual WEB the name is resolved against the materials of the LOADED document - exactly, then ignoring case, first match wins. Unity writes the library material into the exported GLB under exactly this name, so a document exported from Unity always resolves. Empty = not used. It is applied to every renderer under a child named Faces, only while OverrideMaterials is true.

OverrideMaterials.description: Overrides the CAD materials of MantleMesh (MantleMaterialName) and of every renderer under a Faces child (FaceMaterialName) at simulation start; restored at stop. An empty name leaves that part unchanged. Default false.

CoreRadiusMm.description: Radius of the bare core (sleeve). Must be > 0, otherwise the winder is inert with a warning. 76.2 mm is the 3 inch core of the converting industry.

RibbonThicknessMm.description: Thickness of one wound layer of the material, in millimeters (the caliper). With the core radius it decides how fast the roll grows and shrinks. It must be the SAME value as RibbonPath.RibbonThicknessMm - it is the same material - or the roll builds up at a rate the web does not run at. Must be > 0, otherwise the winder is inert with a warning. Default 0.1 mm.

InitialWoundLengthMm.description: How much material is on the roll at the start and after a reset. -1 (the default) means a full roll exactly as modelled - the length is derived from the modelled outer radius, so a full parent reel needs no number typed in. 0 means an empty core, which is what a rewinder starts at. Any other value is the length on the roll in millimeters.

MaxDiameterMm.description: Diameter at which the roll counts as full: the whole web group stops and the Full signal goes true. 0 = no limit.

SpeedControl.description: How this winder decides its own drive speed. A winder is the one roller in a line whose radius moves, so a drive turning at a constant angular speed changes its surface speed as the roll builds or empties - which is what runs a dancer into a stop within a minute. None (the default) leaves the authored drive speed untouched, exactly as before this field existed. LineSpeed holds the winder SURFACE speed at the line speed, omega = line speed / current radius, recomputed every tick. Dancer adds a proportional trim from the carriage position of the dancer beside it, so the store is held near its home position instead of drifting; a winder that has no dancer of its own to regulate on behaves as LineSpeed. In every mode the control writes nothing at all once the drive is commanded from outside - a live signal binding, a recording, or a Drive_FollowPosition wired to the real drive position. The real machine brings its own numbers and the internal control steps aside.

DancerGainPerMm.description: Millimeters per second of surface speed added per millimeter the dancer carriage sits away from its home position, in SpeedControl Dancer. Higher pulls the carriage back to home harder; too high makes it swing around home instead of settling. Capped by MaxTrimPercent. Ignored in the other modes.

MaxTrimPercent.description: How far the dancer trim may move the winder off the line speed, in percent of the line speed, in either direction. It is the safety rail on DancerGainPerMm: a carriage stuck at a stop can then never run the winder away.

RollMesh.description: Which part grows and shrinks with the roll. Leave it empty: the winder object IS the roll and is scaled directly, which is the normal case. Model the core as a SIBLING next to it, never as a child - a child would scale with the paper and the core would visibly grow. Set this only when the roll is a separate part, or when the winder object has no geometry of its own; a winder with nothing to scale gets a plain cylinder so it is never invisible. The modelled scale is remembered and restored on export. Wire componentType UnityEngine.Transform (the schema convention for a node reference).

DiameterMm.description: Signal carrying the current roll diameter in millimeters; written only when it changed by more than 0.1 mm.

WoundLengthMm.description: Signal carrying the currently wound web length in millimeters.

Empty.description: Signal is true while the roll is down to its bare core. An empty winder clamps the web speed of its whole path group to zero.

Full.description: Signal is true once MaxDiameterMm is reached. A full winder clamps the web speed of its whole path group to zero.

RibbonPath.description: One taut web running over an ordered, OPEN chain of rollers (RibbonRoller / RibbonWinder), from the first entry to the last. The reader computes the tangents and wrap arcs itself and builds a band mesh along the resulting arc length; nothing about the path geometry is exported. A slitter is modelled as N RibbonPaths sharing an unwinder: paths that share a winder form ONE group with a single effective speed per tick, so an empty or full roll stops every strip in the same tick.

Rollers.description: Rollers in running order. The first and last entry are the ends of the open path and are usually winders; a winder in the middle makes the path inert.

ConnectedDrive.description: DEPRECATED and IGNORED since plan-460; kept so a plan-459 document still validates. The web is moved exclusively by rotational drives on the rollers: a RibbonRoller or RibbonWinder whose node carries a rotational Drive about the roller axis is driven, and its surface speed v = omega * pi / 180 * r is the speed of its section. Loading a document that still sets this field logs one warning.

SpeedSource.description: DEPRECATED and IGNORED since plan-460; kept so a plan-459 document still validates. See ConnectedDrive: the speed source is now always the driven rollers of the path.

RibbonWidthMm.description: Width of the web, extruded along the common roller axis.

RibbonThicknessMm.description: Thickness of the material, in millimeters. Half of it lifts the web off the roller surface so the two do not intersect. It must be the SAME value as RibbonWinder.RibbonThicknessMm on the winders of this path. Default 0.1 mm.

TextureLengthMm.description: How much web one repetition of the surface pattern covers, in millimeters. This is what makes a running web look like it is running: the pattern scrolls by the distance the web has travelled. A larger value gives a coarser pattern that appears to move more slowly. Default 1000 mm.

SamplesPerMeter.description: How finely the web strip is subdivided, in points per meter of path. Raise it when a tight wrap looks angular; lower it on a very long run to save geometry. Give every strip slit at the same roller the SAME value: the sample points sit on an absolute grid of one point every 1000 / SamplesPerMeter millimeters, which is what lets strips of different total length cut at exactly the same place. A path that grows past its sample buffer has its density reduced automatically (with a console message), which can leave it on a coarser grid than its siblings and move its cut by a fraction of a sample; the console names both webs when that happens, and the fix is a lower SamplesPerMeter for the whole slitter or a shorter longest strip. Default 64.

Material.description: Optional LEGACY node reference. A NODE whose material the web copies - a printed pattern, a coloured film. It points at an object in the scene, not at a material asset: the web takes the first textured material found on that object, including its normal and roughness maps, and gets its own copies of them - scaling and scrolling the web never touches the part it was copied from. MaterialName takes PRECEDENCE over it. Leave both empty and the web gets a plain paper-white surface with a pattern, so its motion is always visible. Wire componentType UnityEngine.Transform (the schema convention for a node reference).

MaterialName.description: Name of a material of the ribbon material library (Unity: Resources/realvirtual/RibbonMaterialLibrary). In realvirtual WEB the name is resolved against the materials of the LOADED document - exactly, then ignoring case, first match wins. Unity writes the library material into the exported GLB under exactly this name, so a document exported from Unity always resolves. Empty = not used. It takes precedence over Material.

SlitAtRoller.description: Optional INNER roller (the cutter) at which the full web is slit into this strip. The cut sits where the web MEETS that roller (its arrival tangent point), which is where the blade is: before it the path draws the full web (FullWidthMm, centred on the first roller), from that point on this strip (RibbonWidthMm) in its own lane at the last roller's axial offset. Every strip cut at the same roller therefore reports the same slit point and draws only itself from there on. Of all strips slit at one roller only the first (by node path) draws the shared part. Requires FullWidthMm > 0.

FullWidthMm.description: Width of the full web before SlitAtRoller; 0 = this path is not a slit strip.

BasisWeightGsm.description: Basis weight of the material in grams per square metre. It normalises the tension into a specific tenacity (N*m/kg), which is what makes two webs of different grammage comparable. Display only - it does not change any force.

TensileStiffnessNPerMmWidth.description: Secant tensile stiffness in MD, in newtons per millimetre of web width at 100 % strain. This is the ONE switch of the whole tension model: 0 (the default) means no tension, no strain, no sag and no colouring - the web behaves exactly as it did before. Read it off the strip tensile curve (EDANA/INDA NWSP 110.4) as a secant at the working point; for a nonwoven there is no Hookean region, so a single modulus is only valid near the tension the machine actually runs at. E times A is deliberately NOT the input: the caliper of a nonwoven is compressible and not uniquely defined.

MinStrainPercent.description: Strain below which the web counts as SLACK, in percent. It raises an alarm and colours the web cyan; it clamps nothing. Default 0, i.e. the web is slack as soon as it is no longer stretched at all.

MaxStrainPercent.description: Strain above which the web counts as OVERSTRETCHED, in percent. It raises an alarm and colours the web magenta; it clamps nothing. A nonwoven runs close to its yield point, so this is a working limit, not the breaking point - that is BreakForceNPer50mm.

BreakForceNPer50mm.description: MD strip tensile force at break, in newtons per 50 mm of width - the number on every nonwoven data sheet. Reaching the strain it implies sets IsBroken and FREEZES the zone's strain until the simulation is reset; it is the only threshold of the model that clamps anything. 0 disables breaking.

TargetTensionNPerM.description: Set-point web tension per unit width, in newtons per metre. The unwinder pays the web out at this tension, so it is the entry strain of the first zone and the value every zone starts and resets at. It is also the centre of the tolerance band the colouring uses. Rules of thumb: 0.3 to 3.0 PLI covers 80 % of all webs (1 PLI = 175.1 N/m); paper 0.5 to 1.0 PLI per mil of caliper, film 0.25 to 0.5; generically 10 to 25 % of the tensile strength.

ToleranceBandPercent.description: Half-width of the good band around TargetTensionNPerM, in percent of it. Inside the band the web is NOT coloured at all - only a deviation is shown, with a hard edge at the band limit, so the normal picture of the machine is the customer's own material.

EnableSag.description: Whether a slack web visibly hangs through. The excess length of a zone with negative strain is distributed over its free spans and drawn as a sag; switching it off leaves the geometry taut while the strain, the signals and the colouring keep reporting the slackness.

TensionColoring.description: Whether the band is tinted by its tension state. Off leaves the material untouched and reports the state through the signals and the readout only.

TintStrength.description: How strongly the tension tint is mixed into the band material, 0 to 1. It scales the deviation colours and the two alarm colours alike; the good band is never tinted whatever this value is.

DeformationScale.description: Visual exaggeration of the sag depth. At the strains a real machine runs, the sag is a fraction of a millimetre and invisible; raising this makes it visible for a demonstration. It multiplies the DEPTH only - tension, strain, signals and the tolerance band are untouched.

ShowTensionLabels.description: Whether the tension overlay is drawn: a readout per zone (N/m, PLI, strain, trend arrow) and, on a loaded dancer, a force arrow with the carriage travel bar.

TensionN.description: Signal carrying the web tension of the LAST zone in newtons. Written only when it changed by more than the equivalent of 0.5 N/m.

SpecificTensionNPerM.description: Signal carrying the tension of the LAST zone per unit width, in newtons per metre - the number a tension controller regulates. Written only on a change of more than 0.5 N/m.

StrainPercent.description: Signal carrying the strain of the LAST zone in percent. Written only on a change of more than 0.01 %.

IsSlack.description: Signal is true while ANY zone of the path is below MinStrainPercent.

IsOverstretched.description: Signal is true while ANY zone of the path is above MaxStrainPercent.

IsBroken.description: Signal is true once ANY zone reached the strain implied by BreakForceNPer50mm. The zone's strain is frozen from then on; only a simulation reset clears it.

RibbonDancer.description: A dancer roller: a RibbonRoller that also TRAVELS along an axis and thereby stores web. It splits its RibbonPath into an upstream and a downstream section at its own departure tangent point and integrates the difference of the two section speeds, L = L + (v_up - v_down) * dt, into a carriage position home + L / Strands. At its stops the limit is directional and never stops a drive: at TravelMaxMm only further filling is prevented (v_up becomes min(v_up, v_down)), at TravelMinMm only further emptying - so the opposite delta always frees it again. Exactly one dancer per path is supported; a dancer at the first or last position of Rollers is ignored with a warning.

RadiusMm.description: Contact radius of the dancer roller. 0 measures it from the mesh bounds in the plane perpendicular to Axis.

Axis.description: Local rotation axis of the roller. Must be parallel to every other roller axis of the path.

RibbonSide.description: Which side of the dancer roller the web runs on. Leave it on Auto: the carriage moves, and Auto follows it by always picking the short wrap. Set Left or Right by hand only for an S-wrap or a wrap of more than 180 degrees. Left and Right are the turning sense seen looking along +Axis. Default Auto.

RotationDirection.description: Ignored. Rotation follows the resolved web contact and roller axis automatically. Set the drive direction to match the contact when authoring a driven roller.

SpinMode.description: How the dancer roller shows its rotation; see RibbonRoller.SpinMode.

MantleMesh.description: Mesh scrolled in SpinMode Texture; see RibbonRoller.MantleMesh.

MantleMaterialName.description: Name of a material of the ribbon material library (Unity: Resources/realvirtual/RibbonMaterialLibrary). In realvirtual WEB the name is resolved against the materials of the LOADED document - exactly, then ignoring case, first match wins. Unity writes the library material into the exported GLB under exactly this name, so a document exported from Unity always resolves. Empty = not used. It is applied to the barrel only while OverrideMaterials is true.

FaceMaterialName.description: Name of a material of the ribbon material library (Unity: Resources/realvirtual/RibbonMaterialLibrary). In realvirtual WEB the name is resolved against the materials of the LOADED document - exactly, then ignoring case, first match wins. Unity writes the library material into the exported GLB under exactly this name, so a document exported from Unity always resolves. Empty = not used. It is applied to every renderer under a child named Faces, only while OverrideMaterials is true.

OverrideMaterials.description: Overrides the CAD materials of MantleMesh (MantleMaterialName) and of every renderer under a Faces child (FaceMaterialName) at simulation start; restored at stop. An empty name leaves that part unchanged. Default false.

TravelAxis.description: The direction the carriage runs in, given in the frame of the object the dancer hangs under - the same axis letters as RibbonRoller.Axis. Place the dancer so that moving along the POSITIVE axis lengthens the web path; that is the direction more material stored points in. Usually perpendicular to Axis, but a guide at an angle is allowed and not checked. Default Y.

TravelMinMm.description: Lower stop relative to HomeMm; must be <= 0. Reaching it sets AtMin and holds the downstream speed at the upstream one, so the store cannot empty further.

TravelMaxMm.description: Upper stop relative to HomeMm; must be >= 0. Reaching it sets AtMax and holds the upstream speed at the downstream one, so the store cannot fill further.

HomeMm.description: Rest position along TravelAxis, relative to the authored node position; 0 means the carriage starts and resets exactly where it was modelled.

Strands.description: How many runs of web pass through the carriage. 1 is a single pass over the roller; 2 is the usual loop that goes down to the carriage and back up again. One millimeter of carriage travel then stores that many millimeters of web. Must be at least 1. Default 2.

ShowTravel.description: Draw the track this carriage runs on: the two end stops, the bar between them and a marker on the carriage itself. Independent of RibbonPath.ShowTensionLabels, which switches the NUMBERS - the travel a dancer has left is a property of the machine and stays readable with every readout turned off. Independent of LoadN too: a purely kinematic dancer has a travel range like any other.

ShowValues.description: Draw this carriage own readout next to it: the force it presses into the web, the tension that makes, and where it sits in its travel. Separate from ShowTravel for the same reason the track is separate from RibbonPath.ShowTensionLabels - the NUMBERS are a readout an operator clears off the picture, the track is how the machine is read. Nothing is drawn while LoadN is 0: an unloaded dancer imposes no tension and a force readout of zero newtons says nothing.

PositionMm.description: Signal carrying the carriage position in millimeters; written only when it changed by more than 0.1 mm. This is the regulated variable a web tension controller reads.

AtMin.description: Signal is true while the carriage sits at TravelMinMm (the store is empty).

AtMax.description: Signal is true while the carriage sits at TravelMaxMm (the store is full).

LoadN.description: Force the loaded carriage presses into the web, in newtons. It is the dancer as a tension SETTER: the force balance at the carriage gives T = LoadN / Strands, which becomes the tension of both neighbouring zones immediately and algebraically. The carriage POSITION keeps following the speed difference alone, so changing the load at equal speeds moves nothing. 0 (the default) is the purely kinematic dancer of plan-460. It needs TensileStiffnessNPerMmWidth > 0 on the path to have any effect.

TensionN.description: Signal carrying the web tension this dancer imposes, in newtons (LoadN / Strands). Written only on a change of more than 0.05 N.

TransportStopper.description: Box collider that stops kinematically transported MUs at contact on accumulating linear conveyors. Moving the collider clear releases the parts; it does not stop the belt drive.

Center.description: Collider center in local glTF coordinates, in millimetres.

Size.description: Positive collider dimensions along local axes, in millimetres.

Zone.description: Web-authored effect box on a node that moves with it: Detect reports occupancy, Block stops kinematically transported MUs at contact, Hold takes MUs off the transport and carries them with the node. An activation (always, a bool signal, or a drive standing inside a position window) switches the effects on and off.

Center.description: Box center in local glTF coordinates, in millimetres.

Size.description: Positive box dimensions along the local axes, in millimetres.

Detect.description: Reports whether an MU occupies the box (or is held by it) while the zone is active.

Block.description: Stops kinematically transported MUs at contact with the box while the zone is active.

Hold.description: Takes MUs inside the box off the transport and carries them with the node while the zone is active.

Activation.description: When the effects act: Always, while ActivationSignal is true (Signal), or while ActivationDrive stands still inside AxisFrom..AxisTo (Axis).

ActivationSignal.description: Bool signal that activates the zone when Activation is Signal.

InvertSignal.description: If true the zone is active while ActivationSignal is false.

ActivationDrive.description: Drive whose position activates the zone when Activation is Axis.

AxisFrom.description: Lower end of the activation window, in millimetres or degrees of ActivationDrive (inclusive).

AxisTo.description: Upper end of the activation window, in millimetres or degrees of ActivationDrive (inclusive).

SignalOccupied.description: Optional bool signal written with the Detect result on every change.

HoldAcquire.description: OnActivate takes the MUs inside the box when the zone becomes active; WhileActive also takes MUs that enter later.

HoldCount.description: All holds every contained MU; One holds at most one MU in total (the one nearest the box center).

GripTargetSearchRadius.description: Search radius in millimetres for a free GripTarget when a held MU is released without a transport surface below it.

ShowGizmo.description: Shows the box in the editor and during a test run.

SingleRelease.description: With Block on a stopper: releases exactly one MU per lowering; the following MU is caught at the raised stopper face even when it touches the released one. Ignored while Hold is on.

CollisionRole.description: Collision role of this node's subtree. Bodies of different roles are checked against each other while the simulation runs; identical roles never collide.

Collision role of this node's subtree. Bodies of different roles are checked against each other; identical roles never collide. 'None' = not checked. 'Cutter' marks a cutting tool: its contact with a workpiece being machined by it is suppressed while the spindle runs.

MachiningVolume.description: Workpiece with real-time CSG material removal: an SDF voxel grid that the listed MachiningTools subtract from every tick (result = max(workpiece, -sweptTool)). The changed 16^3 chunks are re-tessellated into per-chunk meshes. Requires the private machining provider (rv_csg WASM kernel); without it the authored mesh stays untouched.

gridResolution.description: Voxel lattice resolution (x/y/z), including one padding voxel per side. Clamped to 4..256 per axis. Memory and cost scale with the product - 64^3 is the interactive default, 128^3 is usable with a visible mesh lag.

workpieceSize.description: Stock dimensions in millimeters (no coordinate flip - this is an extent, not a position). Ignored when Shape is Mesh, where the domain follows the render geometry's bounds.

Shape.description: Starting stock shape - this defines the MATERIAL, not the display mesh. Mesh voxelizes the node's own render geometry (WYSIWYG); the Unity StockMesh reference is not transferred. Read-only: the bare field name 'Shape' is shared with MachiningTool, so the generic enum editor cannot offer the right options.

CylinderAxis.description: Axis a Cylinder workpiece lies along (X or Z = lying, Y = upright).

Tools.description: MachiningTool references that cut this volume, IN ORDER - the subtraction is sequential, so the order is part of the result.

ToolGroup.description: Optional group name: every MachiningTool whose node carries this group is registered in addition to the explicit Tools list. Leave empty to use only the list.

SweepToolMotion.description: Subtract the swept volume between two ticks so fast feed cuts a continuous groove instead of a dotted line.

MaxSweepSubsteps.description: Upper bound of tool poses sampled per tick along the motion path, per tool. The actual count follows a half-voxel sampling density.

Meshing.description: Surface extraction: MarchingCubes (robust default, edges rounded within one voxel) or DualContouring (sharper edges, experimental).

CreaseAngle.description: Hard-edge threshold in degrees. Incident faces diverging by more than this get a duplicated, unsmoothed vertex. 0 disables crease splitting (fully smooth).

GenerateUVs.description: Generate triplanar UV coordinates for the machined chunk meshes.

StatisticsInterval.description: Seconds between MaterialRemainingPercent refreshes (a full-grid solid-voxel scan).

UpdateCollider.description: Unity-only. realvirtual WEB v1 does not rebuild physics colliders for machined chunks; the flag is shown for parity and has no effect.

SignalSpindleOn.description: Spindle running - material is only removed while this is true. Unbound = always cutting.

SignalReset.description: Rising edge resets the workpiece to its original state (queued cuts are discarded).

SignalMachiningActive.description: Written by the viewer: true while cuts or mesh rebuilds are still outstanding. Momentary state, not a latch.

MachiningTool.description: Cutter geometry for CSG material removal. Pure data - the node's world pose per tick defines where it cuts; a MachiningVolume must list it (or its group) to have any effect.

Shape.description: Cutter shape, evaluated as an analytic signed distance function. Read-only: the bare field name 'Shape' is shared with MachiningVolume, so the generic enum editor cannot offer the right options.

CornerRadius.description: Corner radius in millimeters - used by BallNose and Torus.

TaperAngleDeg.description: Taper half-angle in degrees - used by ConicalEnd.

WebSensor.description: 3D-HMI marker: visualizes a bool or int signal as Low/High/Warning/Error states on the node.

SignalBool.description: Binary input: false = Low, true = High; use for 2-state sensors.

SignalInt.description: Integer input: value mapped to a state via IntStateMap; use for sensors with more states.

IntStateMap.description: Mapping of integer signal values to visual states, e.g. '0=Low;1=High;2=Warning;3=Error'.

Label.description: Optional label shown in the tooltip and sensor list.

Fmu.description: FMI 2.0 Co-Simulation unit attached to a node (web-authored). The .fmu bytes are embedded as a glTF bufferView; the viewer creates one signal child per supported variable and runs the FMU only through realvirtual CONNECT.

AllowViewerToFmu.description: If true the viewer may write the FMU inputs (CONNECT AllowWebToPlc).

FmuEmbed.description: Package metadata: fileName, sha256, guid, modelName, fmiVersion, generationTool, generationDateAndTime, byteLength and the bufferView holding the bytes (-1 = not saved).

FmuVariables.description: Model variables from modelDescription.xml: name, valueReference, causality, variability, type, start, unit, description, initial, min, max, declaredType, enumItems.

FmuStartOverrides.description: Start-value overrides by variable name (value as string). CONNECT applies them when the instance starts; only parameters and inputs are allowed.

FmuUnits.description: UnitDefinitions from modelDescription.xml: unit name to its FMI BaseUnit (exponents m, s, rad, kg, K, A, mol, cd plus factor and offset). The viewer resolves the unit of each FMU signal through it; absent in packages attached before plan-512.

RestartOnReset.description: If true a simulation reset (Play/Reset) restarts the running FMU instance.

WebDiagnostics.description: 3D-HMI marker: couples a PLC error signal to the AI error diagnosis; a rising edge triggers a diagnose request for this node.

DocFilter.description: Metadata filter passed to the diagnosis backend (machine, component or error-code range).

WebSafetyDoor.description: 3D-HMI marker: safety-door overlay with hazard-zone halo and floating label.

LabelHeight.description: Label position above the floor in millimeters.
