KinematicMechanism.description: Container and constraint solver for a closed or open RIGID-BODY kinematic chain built from KinematicJoint components (plan-404). Distinct from the 'Kinematic' component above, which is a hierarchy re-structuring directive for the older axis-group system — a mechanism solves a joint graph with loop closure and free bodies instead. Collects every KinematicJoint in its subtree; actively driven joints (KinematicJoint.DrivenBy) are boundary conditions, all remaining generalized coordinates are solved once per fixed update.

SolverIterations.description: Fixed number of damped Newton-Raphson iterations per tick. Kept constant for determinism.

Damping.description: Damped-least-squares damping factor guarding against Jacobian singularities.

Tolerance.description: Normalized constraint residual tolerance for the Converged flag.

SignalConverged.description: Optional PLC diagnosis signal mirroring Converged.

Converged.description: True when the last solve met Tolerance. Written by the solver.

ResidualError.description: Max normalized constraint residual of the last solve. Written by the solver.

SolveTimeMs.description: Wall-clock duration of the last solve. Written by the solver.

KinematicJoint.description: Declarative, purely kinematic joint connecting two rigid links of a KinematicMechanism (plan-404). No physics involved — pure data consumed by the mechanism solver. Connected links need NOT be parented to each other, which is what makes closed loops expressible.

JointType.description: Constraint kind. Only Revolute (1 rotational DOF about AxisA) and Prismatic (1 translational DOF along AxisA) can become spanning-tree edges; Spherical (3 DOF ball) and Universal (2 DOF cardan) are always loop-closure constraints.

BodyA.description: First connected link. NORMATIVE (plan-404 §2.4): an ABSENT key means the joint is anchored against WORLD/static space — this is the authored world-anchor semantics, not a defect, because the Unity GLB serializer omits null fields entirely. A key that IS present but does not resolve is an error (finding UnresolvedBody), never silently treated as a world anchor.

BodyB.description: Second connected link. Required — a joint always needs a moving link on this side. An absent BodyB yields the MissingBodyB error finding.

AnchorA.description: Joint anchor point in Body A local space.

AnchorB.description: Joint anchor point in Body B local space. Should coincide with AnchorA in world space; a gap beyond tolerance yields the AnchorsApart warning.

AxisA.description: Joint axis in Body A local space (Revolute, Prismatic, Universal). Unused by Spherical.

SecondaryAxisB.description: Second joint axis in Body B local space (Universal/cardan only). Unset on a Universal joint yields the MissingSecondaryAxis warning.

UseLimits.description: If true the joint value is clamped between LowerLimit and UpperLimit. Only Revolute and Prismatic have a single scalar value a limit can clamp.

LowerLimit.description: Lower limit in degrees (Revolute) or millimeters (Prismatic).

UpperLimit.description: Upper limit in degrees (Revolute) or millimeters (Prismatic).

DrivenBy.description: Optional Drive that actively controls this joint value. Absent = passive joint solved by the mechanism.

CurrentValue.description: Current joint value in degrees (Revolute/Universal) or millimeters (Prismatic). Written by the solver.

MechanismBody.description: Rigid-body mass properties of ONE link of a KinematicMechanism, used by the inverse-dynamics force analysis (plan-412). Place it on a link node. Mass, centre of mass and inertia tensor are computed from the geometry the link owns (its subtree minus any other link's subtree) times the effective density; Mass and COM can be overridden. Distinct from JTData.Mass, which is read-only CAD provenance whose unit is not recorded in the file and is therefore only ever offered as a suggestion, never applied automatically. A link WITHOUT this component disables the force analysis for its whole mechanism (the kinematic solve is unaffected).

DensityPreset.description: Material preset the density is taken from. Choose 'custom' to enter DensityKgM3 directly.

DensityKgM3.description: Effective density applied to the computed volume. Follows DensityPreset unless the preset is 'custom'.

MassOverrideKg.description: Optional. Replaces the computed mass entirely; the inertia tensor is scaled with it, so the part keeps its shape and only its density is corrected. Absent = use the computed mass.

ComOverrideLocalMm.description: Optional. Replaces the computed centre of mass, in the link's local space. Absent = use the computed centroid.

InertiaOverrideLocalKgMm2.description: Optional (plan-501). [Ixx,Iyy,Izz,Ixy,Ixz,Iyz] about the centre of mass, link-local axes, kg*mm^2. Replaces the computed tensor after the mass override scaled it. Absent = computed. An invalid value (not 6 finite numbers, not positive definite) is a hard finding: the link is withheld from the force analysis, never silently replaced by the computed tensor.

MassSource.description: How the effective values were obtained: mesh, convex-hull, bounds, override or none. Diagnostic only - written by the analysis.

KinematicTarget.description: Inverse-mode companion of KinematicMechanism (plan-404 Phase 4): drives a mechanism's actively-driven joints so TargetLink follows this node's own Cartesian world position. Position only — no orientation constraint (a parallel platform such as a Delta has no independent orientation DOF).

Mechanism.description: The KinematicMechanism whose driven joints are solved for this target.

TargetLink.description: The mechanism's own link (e.g. a Delta platform) that should track this node's world position.

TrackingActive.description: If true, an inverse solve runs every tick and takes over the mechanism's Drives. Switching it off releases the Drives back to normal forward behavior.

Reachable.description: False when the target lies outside the workspace or a limit was hit — the mechanism still moves to the closest achievable pose (least-squares) instead of freezing.

MechanismTarget.description: Waypoint of a MechanismPath (plan-729): the node's own world position is the position the path's TargetLink origin moves to. Pure configuration; the path owns the motion.

Mechanism.description: Optional KinematicMechanism this waypoint belongs to; absent = inherited from the path.

InterpolationToTarget.description: Motion into this waypoint: Linear (straight Cartesian line, trapezoid profile) or PointToPoint (joint space, synchronised arrival of all driving Drives).

SpeedToTarget.description: Optional override. Linear: path speed in millimeters per second. PointToPoint: factor on the Drives' own speeds. Absent = path default.

WaitForSeconds.description: Dwell time in seconds after the waypoint is reached.

SetSignal.description: Bool signal set when the waypoint is reached and reset when the path leaves it.

WaitForSignal.description: Bool signal the path waits for (true) after the waypoint is reached.

MechanismPath.description: Cartesian path for a KinematicMechanism (plan-729): moves the TargetLink origin through an ordered list of MechanismTarget waypoints, Linear or PointToPoint per waypoint, using the mechanism's inverse solve. An unreachable waypoint stops the path (no silent clamping).

Mechanism.description: The KinematicMechanism whose driving Drives the path moves.

TargetLink.description: The mechanism's own link (e.g. a Delta platform) whose origin follows the path.

Path.description: Ordered list of MechanismTarget references forming the path.

SignalStart.description: Bool signal whose rising edge starts the path.

SignalIsStarted.description: Bool signal that is true while the path runs.

SignalEnded.description: Bool signal set when the path ended regularly (not after a stop on an unreachable waypoint).

LoopPath.description: Restarts the path after it has ended.

SpeedOverride.description: Speed factor for the whole path (Linear and PointToPoint).

LinearSpeedToTarget.description: Linear path speed in millimeters per second.

LinearAcceleration.description: Linear path acceleration and deceleration in millimeters per second squared.

Trajectory.description: Optional MechanismTrajectory (plan-501). Set = the path plays the trajectory's samples back on the simulation clock instead of its waypoint list.

ShowPath.description: Always draws the path in the viewer, not only while the mechanism is selected (plan-511): the waypoints, or the trajectory the path plays.

StartNextPath.description: ComponentReference to the MechanismPath started when this path ends; read raw.

MechanismTrajectory.description: Sampled Cartesian TCP path of a KinematicMechanism plus a payload - one drive-sizing case (plan-501). A sizing run pushes every sample through inverse solve, forward solve and inverse dynamics in the trajectory's own raster and exports velocity, acceleration and drive torque per driven axis. Samples are validated on every input path (import, load, edit, run, playback).

Mechanism.description: The KinematicMechanism the trajectory is sized for. Required.

TargetLink.description: The mechanism link that carries the TCP (a Delta: the platform). Required.

Name.description: Name of the sizing case; prefix of the exported axis files.

Samples.description: Flat [x0,y0,z0, x1,y1,z1, ...] TCP positions in millimetres in the mechanism root frame, uniform raster. 2 to 20000 samples.

SampleIntervalMs.description: Raster of the samples in milliseconds.

Frame.description: Axis convention of the samples: z-up (CAD / robot convention, converted to the viewer's y-up) or y-up (viewer frame).

TcpOffsetMm.description: TCP relative to the TargetLink origin in the link's local frame - the point the samples describe (inverse-solve anchor).

PayloadMassKg.description: Payload carried by the TargetLink, modelled as a point mass.

PayloadOffsetMm.description: Centre of mass of the payload in the TargetLink's local frame.

OutputIntervalMs.description: Row raster of the exported axis files; a whole multiple of SampleIntervalMs.

ShowPath.description: Always draws the path in the viewer, not only while the mechanism is selected (plan-511).

MU.description: Movable Unit marker. A node marked with MU is the template cloned by a Source, or a pre-placed part live from simulation start.

LoadSeatDepth.description: How deep a load may sit below this MU's collider top and still be its load (a part in a jig, a cap over a valve end). 0 = the load rests on the top within 5 mm.

BoxCollider.description: Axis-aligned collider volume in node-local space, used for sensors, transport surfaces, sources and sinks.

center.description: Collider center in Unity node-local coordinates (readers negate X in glTF space).

size.description: Absolute box dimensions in node-local units (no coordinate flip).

LayoutObject.description: Layout-planner marker on a placed library object.

Label.description: Display label of the placed object.

CatalogId.description: Library catalog id the object was placed from.

Locked.description: If true the object is locked against layout edits.

Splat.description: Gaussian-splat placement settings (axis inversion and local-frame crop box).

CropMinX.description: Local-frame crop box minimum X; splats outside the box are culled.

CropMinY.description: Local-frame crop box minimum Y (raise to hide floor noise).

CropMaxY.description: Local-frame crop box maximum Y (lower to hide ceilings).

AASLink.description: Asset Administration Shell link: connects the node to an AAS on a server.

Description.description: Optional description shown in the tooltip header.

ServerUrl.description: Optional AAS server URL; when empty the AASX is loaded from the local aasx/ folder.

WebComponent.description: JavaScript behavior component stored in the GLB: sandboxed script executed by the viewer's QuickJS runtime when scripting is enabled (trust gate).

Active.description: If false the component is parsed but never executed.

ApiVersion.description: Component-SDK contract version the code was written against.

Language.description: Source language of Code; stored code is always conservative JavaScript.

DesSafe.description: Author claim that the script uses only event-driven primitives (checked by the DES lint).

TypeId.description: Library/type identity for reuse, inspector display and statistics.

Code.description: JavaScript source following the global setup(self) contract; empty means no VM is created.

Path.description: WebViewer-native arc-length path (plan-268): a chain of line/arc segments for path-based movement (AGV/FTS, overhead conveyors). parsePathExtras() in rv-path.ts is the executable TS-SSOT for the structured field shapes ('segments', 'successors', 'align'); they are declared here as generic JSON fields so the inspector, the overlay editor and the MCP tools can author them. Detection is coupled to this payload (inner type 'Path' or absent), never to node names.

version.description: Path schema version (migration anchor). Unknown versions parse best-effort with a warning.

id.description: Stable path id for graph edges ('successors') and Agv.PathId. Empty/absent = the carrying node's name.

segments.description: Ordered segment chain in world meters: { kind:'line', from:[x,y,z], to:[x,y,z] } | { kind:'arc', center:[x,y,z], radius, startAngle, degrees, clockwise?, plane?:'XZ'|'XY'|'YZ' }. Unknown kinds are skipped with a warning.

closed.description: Circulating path (overhead conveyor / loop): arc-length addresses wrap modulo length.

successors.description: Path ids this path continues into (graph edges / switches). Dangling ids are tolerated until the referenced path loads.

align.description: Up vector [x,y,z] for the traveler pose (default [0,1,0]).

zone.description: Control-point zone id (mutual exclusion at crossings). Empty/absent = unzoned.

zoneCapacity.description: Explicit zone capacity (>= 0; 0 = never enterable). Absent = default capacity 1.

DrivesRecorder.description: Playback settings for a recorded drive sequence.

PlayOnStart.description: If true playback starts automatically on simulation start.

ReplayStartFrame.description: First frame of the replay range.

ReplayEndFrame.description: Last frame of the replay range; 0 = to end.

Active.description: Connection-state gate: controls playback in connected/disconnected mode.

DrivesRecording_compact.description: Compact drive recording: flat position array indexed as positions[frame * driveCount + driveIndex].

fixedDeltaTime.description: Fixed timestep of the recording in seconds.

drives.description: Array of { id, path } drive descriptors.

sequences.description: Optional array of { name, startFrame, endFrame } named sequences.

positions.description: Flat drive positions array indexed as positions[frame * driveCount + driveIndex].

ReplayRecording.description: Signal-triggered replay of a named sequence from a DrivesRecording.

Sequence.description: Name of the sequence inside the recording to replay.

StartOnSignal.description: Bool signal that starts the replay on a rising edge.

IsReplayingSignal.description: Bool signal set true while the replay is running.

Active.description: Connection-state gate: controls replay in connected/disconnected mode.

Connections.description: Typed, directed connections between components (plan-259). Carried once per scene (typically on the root node) under extras.realvirtual.Connections. A connection is a named bidirectional call: the source invokes the target with request parameters, the target answers (usually deferred) with response parameters.

connections.description: Flat edge list (serialization truth; adjacency is a runtime index). 1:n fan-out/fan-in via repeated source/target paths.

connectionTypes.description: User-defined connection type signatures. Built-in types (StopOnExit) are registered in code and need no entry.

RvConnection.description: One directed connection edge between two nodes, identified by scene paths.

id.description: Stable edge id, unique within the scene.

source.description: Slash-separated node path of the source (caller) end.

target.description: Slash-separated node path of the target (callee) end.

type.description: Connection type name — built-in (StopOnExit) or user-defined via connectionTypes.

config.description: Type-specific per-edge configuration, e.g. { ProcessTime: 3.0 } for StopOnExit.

ConnectionType.description: User-defined connection type signature: request/response parameter schemas. Makes a GLB self-describing — the viewer renders typed inspector fields and validates call parameters without any code.

request.description: Request parameter schema: parameter name to wire type (bool | int | float | string).

response.description: Response parameter schema: parameter name to wire type (bool | int | float | string).

AssetReference.description: Marks the node as a REFERENCE NODE: its subtree is not stored in this file but in another glTF/GLB asset, which a consumer resolves and grafts under this node (composition). Resolution order is normative: (1) 'assetId' through the consumer's asset resolver; (2) 'path', resolved RELATIVE TO THE FILE THE REFERENCE IS WRITTEN IN — never relative to the root scene of a composition; (3) otherwise the reference is UNRESOLVED and the node stays empty, which a consumer MUST report and MUST NOT treat as an error that aborts the load. 'sha256' is a change DETECTOR only and MUST NOT be used as a resolution key: a reference resolves to the CURRENT bytes of the asset so corrections in a library reach every referencing file. A consumer MUST bound recursion (cycle detection along the resolution path, plus a depth limit) and MUST NOT treat repeated use of the same asset on DIFFERENT paths as a cycle - that is a DAG and legitimate.

assetId.description: Primary, location-independent identity of the referenced asset. Survives moving and renaming the file.

providerId.description: Optional id of the provider/resolver the assetId belongs to (library, project, catalog).

sourceId.description: Optional id of the source within the provider (a specific library source).

path.description: Fallback locator, relative to the file this reference is written in. Used only when assetId does not resolve.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the referenced bytes as of the last save. Change DETECTION only, never a resolution key; a mismatch means the referenced asset was updated and is reported as such.

embedded.description: True when a flat export inlined the referenced subtree into this file. The reference is then a provenance note; consumers MUST NOT resolve it again.

AssetOverrides.description: Sits on the SAME node as an AssetReference and carries what THIS file changes in the referenced subtree. The referenced file is never modified. Each patch is an RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch over 'extras.realvirtual' of the target node - componentType to fieldName to value, where null DELETES the field. Addressing is by the target node's reserved 'NodeId' key, which is unique WITHIN the referenced file; the occurrence a node belongs to comes from the chain of reference nodes at composition time and is never written into a file, so the same asset may be referenced any number of times and each occurrence is overridden independently. An override whose target no longer exists is ORPHANED: consumers MUST report it and MUST NOT discard it silently. Strength ordering when several layers touch one field, weakest first: values in the referenced file, then overrides of the inner referencing file, then overrides of the outer referencing file, then the running session's edit log - the outer file always wins.

byNodeId.description: NodeId of a node in the referenced subtree to an RFC 7396 merge patch over that node's extras.realvirtual.

byPath.description: Fallback addressing for targets without a NodeId: node path RELATIVE TO THE REFERENCE NODE to the same merge-patch shape. Consulted only after byNodeId misses.

SceneCamera.description: Authored camera start preset of the scene, written on the scene root node. Field-identical to the ModelCameraStart preset a viewer keeps per model, so moving a preset into the file (or back out) loses nothing. Positions and target are in the file's own coordinate system. A consumer MUST reject the preset when any of the six coordinates is not finite.

duration.description: Tween duration when moving to the preset, in seconds; consumers clamp to [0.05, 60].

savedAt.description: Wall-clock timestamp (milliseconds since the Unix epoch) the preset was saved, for display only.

source.description: Origin of the preset: 'author' when it came with the file, 'user' when a viewer user saved it.

PlacementMeta.description: Marks the node as a LAYOUT PLACEMENT and carries the placement data an AssetReference cannot express. Its PRESENCE is normative: a consumer MUST treat a node carrying PlacementMeta as a placement of the containing scene and MUST NOT treat a reference node without it as one - that is how a placement is told apart from a reference an author wrote by hand. A placement node also carries the reserved 'NodeId' key, which is the placement's stable identity: a writer re-saving a scene MUST update the node with the matching NodeId in place rather than append a second one. A GAUSSIAN SPLAT placement carries NO AssetReference at all (a reference points at a glTF asset by definition) and puts its catalog identity in 'catalogId' instead. 'visible' lives here because glTF has no visibility flag, so a hidden placement would otherwise come back visible on the next load.

catalogId.description: Catalog entry id of the placed asset. Written ONLY when the node carries no AssetReference to hold it (the splat case); otherwise AssetReference.assetId is the single source of truth.

splatUrl.description: Source of the Gaussian splat this placement renders. When set, the placement has no glTF asset and the node carries no AssetReference.

visible.description: False when the user hid the placement. Absent means visible.

signalMappings.description: Live-signal bindings of this placement, stored verbatim. Each entry describes one binding: 'signal' (the signal name at the provider, or the model signal name), 'sourceKind' ('connect' or 'internal'; absent means 'connect'), 'direction' (PLC direction - read-only output vs. writable input), 'enabled', and optionally 'id', 'interfaceId' and 'topic'. A consumer MUST round-trip unknown members of an entry unchanged rather than normalise them away.

SceneSettings.description: Workspace settings of a scene, written on the scene root node. These belong to the scene as a whole rather than to any node: the library catalogues its placements are drawn from, and the layout grid it was laid out on. A consumer that finds no SceneSettings block MUST fall back to its own defaults; an ABSENT field means 'the file has no opinion' and MUST NOT be confused with a field carrying the default value, because only the former may be overridden by a user preference.

physicsEnabled.description: Opts this scene into zone physics in an internal viewer; absent keeps the viewer preference.

catalogUrls.description: Library catalogue URLs the scene draws its placements from.

gridSizeMm.description: Layout grid and translation snap step, in millimetres.

ConnectionMode.description: Simulation / PLC start mode of a model (one per model, on a dedicated node). Simulation starts the viewer disconnected, so logic roots with Active Disconnected (a virtual PLC) run; PLC starts it connected. Without this component the viewer keeps its default (connected). A live interface connection overrides the mode; on disconnect the viewer returns to StartMode.

StartMode.description: Mode at load: Simulation = connection state Disconnected (virtual PLC runs), PLC = Connected (a real PLC owns the outputs).

WebOperatorPanel.description: 3D-HMI marker: an operator panel window (illuminated push buttons, selector switches, E-stops, stack light, status line) described as JSON. Every WebOperatorPanel of a model opens one window; buttons write PLC inputs, lamps show PLC outputs. No Unity runtime function.

Title.description: Window title; empty uses the title in Config.

Config.description: The operator panel as a JSON string (version, id, title, buttons, selectors, estops, stackLight, chips, status, restart). Must parse and validate; every signal it names must exist in the model.

Dock.description: Screen corner the window first appears in when Config has no position; several panels in one corner stack.

StartCollapsed.description: If true the window starts collapsed to its title bar (chips, stack light and the E-stop stay reachable).
